text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Privatisation of state-owned companies has raised almost 10 billion markka.
- UPM-Kymmene's French owned Straceli pulp factory losses last year reached record high, 155 million markka, amid low pulp prices.
- Leftist Alliance must stay in the government, says Pekka Ahmavaara, director of Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK).
- Finland is believed to have given refuge to a handful of Chinese political dissidents.
- Temporary food banks have become permanent relief for many poor and long-term unemployed.
- Finnish construction business in Russia will grow strongly in the next two years, by 600-800 million markka, sector representatives say.
- Post as well as telecoms operator Telecom Finland should be listed on the stock exchange, post and tele managing director Pekka Vennamo says.
- Swedish major industry figure Percy Barnevik might seek to link Stora to the Finland's UPM Kymmene, a Swedish pulp technology professor says.
- New media -- multimedia and Internet WWW services -- has become strongest growth industry.
- New name of merged Aamulehti and MTV media company will probably be decided by mid-June, says Ahti Martikainen, head of communication at Aamulehti.
- Transport is on the brink of overheating, sector representatives say.
- Trade union youth organisations critizise trend of "enforced training" produced by labour market reform.
